staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The staged patch removes caller-side `xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler)` cleanup from multiple HTML save helpers and changes `xmlIO.c` so output-buffer constructors consume encoder ownership even on error.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is a heap-use-after-free read in `xmlCharEncCloseFunc`. `htmlSaveFileFormat` passes an encoding handler into `xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename`; on this failing path the callee frees that handler during `xmlOutputBufferClose(ret)`, returns `NULL`, and the caller immediately calls `xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler)` again on the dangling pointer.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in libxml2's encoding cleanup: xmlCharEncCloseFunc (encoding.c) is invoked on an encoding handler that has already been freed during HTML output processing (htmlSaveFileFormat in HTMLtree.c / xmlOutputBufferClose in xmlIO.c). This leads to reads from freed heap memory, causing crashes or memory corruption and presenting a potential security risk when processing crafted HTML/XML input (e.g., via xmllint).
bug_description.normalized: The 24-byte staged testcase is not a normal standalone HTML file; it is an OSS-Fuzz `fuzz/lint.c` input that decodes into `xmllint` options. Static decoding of the saved `poc` shows the witness sets `--auto`, `--html`, and a one-byte `--encode " "` string, leaving `xmlout` unset. `xmllintMain` therefore reaches the HTML-output path in `parseAndPrintFile()` and calls `htmlSaveFileFormat(..., encoding, 0)` with the attacker-controlled encoding string. `htmlFindOutputEncoder()` converts that non-default encoding name into a heap-allocated extra handler, matching the saved allocation stack in `encoding.c:798`. `xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename()` then aliases that same handler into `ret->encoder`; on the witnessed failing path its `ret->context` remains `NULL`, so `__xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename()` calls `xmlOutputBufferClose(ret)`, which frees the handler once. Vulnerable `htmlSaveFileFormat()` treats `buf == NULL` as if the handler were still caller-owned and invokes `xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler)` again. The second close dereferences the freed handler at `encoding.c:1920`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read. The patch fixes the ownership mismatch from both ends: it removes the duplicate caller-side close sites in `HTMLtree.c` and makes `xmlAllocOutputBuffer()` consume encoder ownership consistently even on internal allocation failures.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled data into the encoder-lifetime state later passed to `htmlSaveFileFormat`.
source.value_from: Decoding the saved 24-byte `poc` with the staged `fuzz/lint.c` / `xmlFuzzReadString` logic yields `--encode " "`, so this statement stores the exact one-byte encoding name `" "` in xmllint's global `encoding` variable.

sink.description: Crash sink. The second `xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler)` call dereferences the already-freed handler to inspect `handler->flags`, producing the saved heap-use-after-free read.

root_cause.description: Caller-side ownership bug on the witnessed path. After `xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename(filename, handler, 0)` has already consumed and freed `handler` during its `NULL` return path, vulnerable `htmlSaveFileFormat()` closes the same handler again.

tainted_value_origin.description: The dangling handler originates from the attacker-controlled `--encode` string parsed here.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admission gate for the witness decoded from the saved `poc`. Static decoding shows the testcase sets `--auto`, and the later `if (generate) parseAndPrintFile(NULL, NULL);` path in `xmllintMain` reaches this `filename == NULL` auto-generation branch before the HTML serialization path executes.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzed xmllint options store a one-byte `--encode` string, enable HTML output, and reach the `htmlSaveFileFormat(..., encoding, 0)` branch.
The attacker-controlled encoding name is resolved into a heap-allocated encoding handler that `htmlSaveFileFormat` passes into filename-output buffer creation.
The output buffer stores the handler in `ret->encoder`, then on the failing creation path closes `ret` and frees that handler before returning `NULL`.
Vulnerable caller cleanup closes the freed handler a second time, and `xmlCharEncCloseFunc` dereferences freed memory while testing `handler->flags`.

fine_trace.note: Source. xmllint stores the attacker-controlled `--encode` argument in the global `encoding` variable. For the saved testcase, the decoded value is the one-byte string `" "`.

The witness-controlled option state reaches the HTML serializer path: `--html` makes `html` nonzero, `--xmlout` is absent, and the non-empty `encoding` string selects the `htmlSaveFileFormat(..., encoding, 0)` call seen in the saved ASan stack.

The attacker-controlled encoding name is resolved into an output handler. On this witness the name is not a built-in static UTF-8/HTML case, so `xmlOpenCharEncodingHandler()` reaches `xmlFindExtraHandler()` and allocates a heap-backed handler, matching the saved allocation stack at `encoding.c:798`.
The caller passes the same handler pointer into output-buffer creation. From this point the callee can alias that pointer into its internal buffer object.
Output-buffer allocation stores the caller's handler pointer in `ret->encoder`, creating the callee-owned alias that later cleanup will free.

On the witnessed failing path, filename-output setup leaves `ret->context == NULL`, so the constructor immediately closes the partially initialized buffer before returning `NULL`. The saved free stack proves this branch executed on the crashing run, although the exact I/O subreason is not recoverable from the staged artifacts alone.
Cleanup frees the handler once through the callee-owned alias stored in `out->encoder`. This is the freeing action reported in the saved ASan backtrace before control returns to `htmlSaveFileFormat`.

Root cause. The caller treats `buf == NULL` as if `handler` were still live and caller-owned, even though step 7 already freed the same object during the callee's error cleanup. This creates the stale-pointer second close.
Sink. The second close in step 8 re-enters `xmlCharEncCloseFunc` with a dangling pointer, and the initial `handler->flags` test performs the saved heap-use-after-free read.

format.name: libxml2 OSS-Fuzz lint testcase
format.contract: The witness is exactly the staged 24-byte `fuzz/lint.c` input whose option-decoding yields `--html`, `--auto`, and a non-empty one-byte `--encode` string `" "`, with an empty main URL. Those concrete settings are sufficient evidence for this sample; the staged artifacts do not prove that neighboring flag or encoding combinations take the same failing ownership path.
